topic_or_scope: Orchestrator rewrite transfer-fidelity audit, legacy-canon cleanup readiness, and reconciliation prep

Keep requested/effective account identity aligned across Contracts, Executor, chat, subagent, interview, and usage surfaces.

notes: The unresolved owner defect is now two-part: the exact `### 5.1B Persona/Runtime Snapshot Payload Contract` anchor is still absent, and the explicit `execution_unit_context` required-field list in `Plans/Contracts_V0.md` still omits `requested_account_binding`, `requested_account_policy`, and `operational_identity` even though surrounding canon expects them.

required_behavior: Keep runtime-artifact identity row-based and storage-owned.
Preserve historical truth after live worktree cleanup instead of collapsing cleanup state into disappearance.
Expose project-state and projection-health semantics consistently to consuming UI surfaces.
notes: This item preserves both key families and lifecycle semantics.

The audit confirmed real storage transfer for `artifacts_index.v1:{project_id}:{artifact_id}`, `historical_lineage_refs[]`, and the broader `project_summary.v1:{project_id}` record family, but the exact `orchestrator.project_state.{project_id}` key and the lifecycle boundary semantics remain unresolved.

The live owner text still exposes only inline `Canonical records for this feature set...` prose plus `canonical_record.v1:{project_id}:{record_id}` rather than a discoverable `Canonical records` heading, and both `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md` and `Plans/Contracts_V0.md` still point at that missing anchor.

`Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md` and `Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md` also still point at the missing `Plans/storage-plan.md#Restart and stale history` anchor, so the unresolved storage defect now includes broken consumer cross-references as well as missing owner headings.
Stale `artifact_kind` and `task_id` references still survive in consumer docs and must retire, but they are not the core owner-shape defect.

required_behavior: Keep receipt records lineage-bearing rather than loosely referential.
Carry exact bridge fields into downstream artifact, interview, and usage consumers.
Preserve validation lineage as concrete fields, not summary prose.
notes: This item is focused on bridge-field and validation-lineage completeness.

The audit confirmed inline receipt transfer for `run_id`, `provider_attempt_ref`, `usage_event_ref`, `workflow_run_id`, `workflow_refs`, `docker_refs`, `kubernetes_refs`, and `validation lineage` in `Plans/storage-plan.md`.

The audit also confirmed that `pass_verdict`, `phase_plan_ref`, and `requirements_quality_report_ref` already live in `Plans/Project_Output_Artifacts.md` as validation-pass-report lineage rather than missing receipt fields.

The unresolved defect is now the missing `### Cross-surface receipt record` owner heading plus the missing consumer anchors for drill-through, validation lineage, bridge-field viewing, and validation/report display.

`Plans/Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md` still points directly at the missing `Plans/storage-plan.md#Cross-surface receipt record` anchor, so the receipt blocker now includes live broken consumer linkage in addition to missing headings.

required_behavior: Keep blocked episodes restart-restorable and action-preserving across chat and HITL surfaces.
Use one shared escalation ladder across tools, approvals, and usage observability.
Retire generic ask-flow payloads that omit blocked-episode identity.
notes: The stale self-verdict in assistant chat must be retired rather than preserved beside open blockers.

The audit confirmed that `report_ref` and `startup_recovered` are already owned elsewhere, but the live `blocked_notice` payload still carries only `blocked_family` and `allowed_action_ids[]`, the usage observability section still reports blocked attempts only by `blocked_reason_code` without `escalation_level`, `action_available` still lacks a discoverable owner, and the ask-tuple schema still is not propagated cleanly.

required_behavior: Instantiate rewrite, routing, and historical entries using the help-entry contract.
Keep confusion-pair and related-concept treatment explicit rather than implied.
Carry stable terms across glossary, inline help, and context help surfaces.
notes: This item captures the three-part help architecture.

The audit confirmed that `Plans/Glossary.md` already carries the required help-entry field template, labels, and many canonical terms, but the named owner headings and populated help-entry rows are still missing.

The live glossary still instantiates terms as two-column `Term | Definition` tables or inline bullets instead of the full help-entry field set (`canonical_name`, `short_definition`, `why_it_matters`, `what_it_is_not`, `common_related_states`, `related_concepts`, `surface_examples`).

`Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md` history and concern sections still point at the missing `Plans/Glossary.md#Orchestrator rewrite terms` anchor, so the consumer side now carries live broken glossary references in addition to the missing owner headings.

required_behavior: Keep Orchestrator as the why/coordination surface beside worktree-first Source Control.
Make current-vs-historical behavior discoverable and explicit.
Separate health, activity, and attention instead of collapsing them into one indicator.
notes: This item is now purely a structural-heading and cross-reference integrity defect rather than a restore-point vocabulary contradiction.

The audit confirmed substantial transfer for worktree-first and health/activity/attention semantics, but the owner headings remain structurally weak, and the non-existent `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md#11. Source Control boundary` reference still survives in `Plans/GitHub_Integration.md`, `Plans/storage-plan.md`, and `Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md`.

`Plans/storage-plan.md` now cleanly separates runtime safe points from project-scoped restore points, and `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` explicitly forbids presenting safe points as restore points, so the prior `restore points` contradiction is no longer part of the unresolved canon defect.
